title: Trace what survives when a request stops being useful
description: Inject a failure, choose a cancellation contract, and size the work queue. The model follows accepted work through admission, workers, and the downstream call.

incidents.label: Client deadline expires
incidents.detail: The caller gives up while jobs are queued and workers are waiting on a dependency.

incidents.label: Downstream latency spike
incidents.detail: A normally fast dependency stalls long enough for producers to outrun the worker pool.

incidents.label: Producer burst
incidents.detail: Traffic jumps briefly while dependency latency remains inside the request deadline.

strategies.label: Detached goroutines
strategies.detail: Start work with a background context and let producers wait for queue space.

strategies.label: Workers check context
strategies.detail: Workers stop downstream calls, but producers can still block while handing work to the queue.

strategies.label: Structured cancellation
strategies.detail: Admission, channel sends, workers, and dependencies all select on the same context.

notice: The lab uses deterministic queue math to expose ownership mistakes. Production systems also need measured latency distributions, retry behavior, dependency quotas, and shutdown tests with the race detector.
